report.incidentSummary: Starting around 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC) on 2026-09-25, users querying the AI assistant about their investments were told they have no holdings, while the Portfolio screen showed accurate holdings. Between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, user-context-service experienced transient timeouts while fetching holdings data. On timeout, user-context-service executed fallback logic that cached empty records ('holdings=0 sips=0') in the shared cache with a 6-hour TTL (21600 seconds). Subsequent assistant queries for those affected users hit these poisoned negative cache entries, causing persistent zero-holdings responses even after the upstream timeouts ceased.
report.rootCauseStatement: user-context-service wrote empty fallback contexts ('holdings=0 sips=0') into the Redis cache keyspace with an excessive 6-hour (21600s) TTL during a transient upstream fetch timeout period between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC. Subsequent requests to user-context-service hit the poisoned cache entries, returning zero holdings to assistant-orchestrator even though portfolio-service was healthy.

hypotheses.cause: During a transient timeout period fetching holdings from portfolio-service, user-context-service cached empty fallback records (holdings=0, sips=0) into the cache keyspace with a 6-hour TTL (21600s), poisoning the context cache for affected users.
hypotheses.rationale: Logs in ev_10 and ev_12 show user-context-service directly executing 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)' on timeout. ev_2 demonstrates missing_context_rate spiked during the 08:50-09:22 UTC timeout window and remained elevated at ~8% through 11:45 UTC due to the 6-hour TTL. Meanwhile, ev_16 confirms portfolio-service latency remained normal, explaining why the Portfolio screen is unaffected.

hypotheses.cause: Ongoing upstream portfolio-service failure or persistent connection degradation between assistant-orchestrator and user-context-service.
hypotheses.rationale: user-context-service error rates returned to baseline (~0.3%) by 09:25 UTC (ev_1), assistant-orchestrator error rates remained steady at ~0.5% throughout (ev_14), and portfolio-service p95 latency remained normal at 118-151 ms (ev_16), contradicting any ongoing portfolio-service outage.

hypotheses.cause: assistant-orchestrator software deployment regression or prompt/tool schema bug causing dropped context.
hypotheses.rationale: No releases or config changes were deployed to assistant-orchestrator on 2026-09-25 (ev_5). The orchestrator experienced no context-retrieval errors or abnormal error rate increases (ev_6, ev_8, ev_9, ev_14).

facts.statement: No deployments or config changes were performed on assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache on 2026-09-25 prior to or during the incident.
user-context-service error_rate spiked from baseline ~0.3% to over 10% between 08:50 UTC and 09:20 UTC, returning to normal baseline (~0.3%) by 09:25 UTC.
user-context-service logged 193 instances of 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready' between 08:50:18 UTC and 09:21:57 UTC.
On context build timeout, user-context-service executed 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)' writes into the shared cache.
user-context-service missing_context_rate jumped from 0.8% to 20.46% at 09:05 UTC and remained continuously elevated between 7% and 8.7% through 11:45 UTC.
portfolio-service p95 latency remained normal and steady between 118.6 ms and 151.8 ms throughout the entire window.
Cache hit rate in the user_context keyspace increased from ~94.8% prior to 08:50 UTC to ~98.5%-99.2% after 09:10 UTC and remained elevated through 11:45 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator error rate stayed flat at ~0.50% across the incident with no context-related log warnings or errors.

inferences.statement: The prolonged nature of the incident ('not going away') despite transient timeout resolution at 09:22 UTC is directly caused by the 6-hour (21600-second) TTL set on fallback empty contexts.

Only users who triggered context builds during the 08:50 to 09:22 UTC timeout window had their cache entries poisoned, explaining why the symptom affected 'some users' rather than the entire user base.
portfolio-service itself was functioning correctly, allowing users on the Portfolio screen to view their investments normally while assistant responses were degraded by the cached fallback context.

assumptions.statement: The assistant orchestrator directly incorporates the user context holdings payload from user-context-service into its prompt without independent holdings re-verification.

timeline.event: knowledge-index deployed CHG-48223; user-context-service and assistant-orchestrator operating at normal baseline.
Onset of timeouts: user-context-service begins experiencing context build timeouts on holdings fetch and writes empty fallback records ('holdings=0 sips=0') to Redis with ttl=21600s.
user-context-service error_rate peaks at 10.32% and missing_context_rate peaks at 20.46%.
Last timeout and fallback write logged by user-context-service; transient timeout window ends.
user-context-service error_rate returns to baseline (~0.31%), but missing_context_rate remains elevated at ~8% due to cached empty fallback records.
Incident INC-3320 reported by Support team lead as assistant continues to report zero holdings for affected users.
Investigation window closes; missing_context_rate persists at 8.03% with elevated cache hit rate (~99%) as poisoned keys have not expired.

confidence.rationale: Direct log evidence shows the exact fallback operation caching holdings=0 with a 21600-second TTL at the exact onset timestamp, correlating directly with the sustained 8% missing_context_rate and the lack of latency degradation in portfolio-service.

gaps.description: Direct inspection of individual Redis keys in the user_ctx keyspace to check remaining TTL and exact payloads.
gaps.impact: Minimal; user-context-service application logs explicitly record the exact Redis SET command string, key format, payload, and TTL.

gaps.description: Root cause of the initial transient connection/readiness failure between user-context-service and portfolio-service pods during 08:50-09:22 UTC.
gaps.impact: Minor for immediate mitigation (flushing cache and fixing TTL bug), but relevant for preventing future upstream transient timeouts.

recommendedActions.action: Purge or invalidate poisoned user_ctx:* keys in Redis that were written between 08:50 UTC and 09:22 UTC with fallback zero holdings.
recommendedActions.rationale: Eliminates remaining poisoned cache entries immediately, allowing affected users to fetch live holdings from portfolio-service.
recommendedActions.verification: Check user-context-service missing_context_rate metric drops from ~8% back to baseline (<1%) and verify assistant correctly answers holdings queries for affected users.

recommendedActions.action: Update user-context-service fallback behavior to either avoid caching negative fallback responses entirely or set a short TTL (e.g. 15-30 seconds) on timeout fallbacks.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents transient downstream or network hiccups from poisoning user context cache for 6 hours.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate timeout in staging and verify fallback cache entries have a short TTL and do not persist across normal queries once connectivity restores.

recommendedActions.action: Investigate pod readiness and network connection pool between user-context-service and portfolio-service during 08:50-09:22 UTC.
recommendedActions.rationale: Underlying logs indicated '# of # pods ready' and holdings fetch pending timeouts; identifying why pods became unready will prevent recurring transient spikes.
recommendedActions.verification: Review Kubernetes pod events, container restart metrics, and gRPC/HTTP client timeout configurations.

incident.title: Assistant cannot see user holdings
incident.summary: Since mid-afternoon (about 14:20 IST) the assistant tells some users it cannot find any holdings. The Portfolio screen is fine. Not going away.
symptoms: assistant claims user holds no funds
incident.userImpact: Wrong personal answers from the assistant; users worry their investments are gone.

payload.question: Propose candidate causes before any evidence

candidates.cause: A recent deployment or release of user-context-service introduced a bug in parsing or serializing portfolio holdings into the context payload, causing it to return empty holdings to the orchestrator.
candidates.whyPlausible: The Portfolio screen queries portfolio-service directly and works normally, whereas the assistant reads holdings adapted by user-context-service. If user-context-service has a parsing or mapping bug, only the assistant's view of holdings is affected.
candidates.wouldConfirm: Deployment logs or version changes on user-context-service around 08:50 UTC (14:20 IST) coinciding with a sharp rise in missing_context_rate or empty context responses in user-context-service logs.
candidates.wouldRuleOut: No deployments or changes to user-context-service around that time, and user-context-service logs show complete, populated holdings payloads being returned to assistant-orchestrator.

candidates.cause: A deployment or prompt template change in assistant-orchestrator fails to inject the user context into the prompt or misinterprets the retrieved context payload.
candidates.whyPlausible: The reporter specifically suspects assistant-orchestrator. A regression in orchestrator's context assembly logic could omit holdings data when querying the LLM provider, leading the LLM to inform users they have no holdings.
candidates.wouldConfirm: A deployment or config change event on assistant-orchestrator near 08:50 UTC, and prompt payloads logged by assistant-orchestrator showing missing holdings sections despite user-context-service returning valid data.
candidates.wouldRuleOut: No deployment or configuration updates to assistant-orchestrator around the onset time, or outgoing LLM prompt logs showing the holdings context was never received from user-context-service.

candidates.cause: Calls from assistant-orchestrator to user-context-service (or user-context-service to portfolio-service) are timing out, triggering a graceful degradation fallback that executes the LLM call without personal holdings.
candidates.whyPlausible: assistant-orchestrator has a tight 1200ms timeout with 0 retries to user-context-service. If user-context-service experiences latency spikes, the orchestrator may fall back gracefully to avoid failing user chat requests, producing answers stating no holdings could be found.
candidates.wouldConfirm: An elevated timeout count or latency_p95_ms on assistant-orchestrator's calls to user-context-service starting around 08:50 UTC, alongside logs indicating context retrieval fallback.
candidates.wouldRuleOut: Latency and timeout metrics between assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, and portfolio-service remain consistently well below their respective timeouts (e.g. <100ms) with zero timeout events.

candidates.cause: Stale or corrupted empty holdings records are cached in the cache keyspace used by user-context-service.
candidates.whyPlausible: user-context-service caches user context in the shared cache. If an invalidation bug or bad payload was written into the user context keyspace, the service would serve empty holdings repeatedly without fetching fresh records from portfolio-service.
candidates.wouldConfirm: Cache inspect/logs showing keys in the user context keyspace populated with empty or malformed holdings objects starting around 08:50 UTC, with normal hit rates on user-context-service.
candidates.wouldRuleOut: user-context-service cache hit rate drops to zero or cache reads return non-empty valid user context objects, or bypassing the cache reproduces the issue identically.

findings.summary: During the investigation window (08:15 to 11:45 UTC), assistant-orchestrator experienced no logged errors, timeouts, or fallback logic related to requesting user context. Its overall error_rate remained steady at baseline (~0.50%). Its only logged errors were 4 tool-call schema validation failures, and warnings were 4 LLM token truncations. assistant-orchestrator does not log raw context payloads or prompt contents, so the exact payload received could not be determined from its logs. Evidence indicates assistant-orchestrator is not failing its context requests; the issue is likely upstream in user-context-service.

observations.statement: assistant-orchestrator logged a total of 168 log records between 08:15:00Z and 11:45:00Z: 160 INFO, 4 WARN, and 4 ERROR. None of the warnings or errors relate to user context retrieval, timeouts, or fallback logic.

The 4 WARN logs in assistant-orchestrator are 'response truncated at max tokens', and the 4 ERROR logs are 'tool-call arguments failed schema validation; regenerating turn'. No context retrieval errors or fallback invocations were logged.
Log queries for 'context' in assistant-orchestrator returned 0 records across the entire investigation window.
assistant-orchestrator error_rate remained baseline between 0.38% and 0.57% (mean ~0.50%) throughout 08:15:00Z to 11:45:00Z, with no error spike at or after 08:50:00Z (14:20 IST).

assistant-orchestrator did not experience errors, timeouts, or fallback triggers when communicating with user-context-service; any issue with missing holdings context likely originates within user-context-service returning empty/degraded context or failing silently upstream.

gaps.description: assistant-orchestrator does not log user context payloads or LLM prompt bodies in its application logs, so the exact context payload received and passed to the LLM could not be retrieved from assistant-orchestrator logs directly.
Ran out of tool budget before querying user-context-service or trace details to inspect upstream context payload generation.

findings.summary: user-context-service experienced a transient error and timeout spike between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC while portfolio-service latency remained normal (~120-150ms). When holdings fetches timed out, user-context-service wrote fallback empty contexts ('holdings=0 sips=0') into the shared cache with a 6-hour TTL (21600s). As a result, subsequent assistant requests hit the cached empty holdings records, keeping missing_context_rate elevated at ~8% and causing the assistant to report zero holdings.

observations.statement: user-context-service error_rate spiked from a baseline of ~0.3% up to 10.32% between 08:50Z and 09:20Z, returning to baseline (~0.3%) by 09:25Z.
user-context-service missing_context_rate spiked from ~0.8% to 20.46% at 09:05Z, then remained continuously elevated between 7% and 8.7% through the end of the window (11:45Z).

user-context-service logs show 193 instances of 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready' between 08:50:18Z and 09:21:57Z, followed by 'cache SET user_ctx:<user_id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'.
portfolio-service latency_p95_ms remained normal and stable throughout the window, ranging between 118.6ms and 151.8ms with no latency spike.
Cache hit rate for the user_context keyspace increased from ~94.8% prior to 08:50Z to ~98.5%-99.2% from 09:10Z onwards and remained elevated through 11:45Z.

During the transient timeout period (08:50-09:22Z), user-context-service wrote empty fallback contexts (holdings=0, sips=0) into cache with a 6-hour TTL (21600s). Consequently, even after errors subsided at 09:25Z, requests for those users continue hitting cached zero-holdings contexts, explaining why missing_context_rate remains elevated at ~8% and assistant claims users have no holdings.

output.incidentSummary: Starting around 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC) on 2026-09-25, users querying the AI assistant about their investments were told they have no holdings, while the Portfolio screen showed accurate holdings. Between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, user-context-service experienced transient timeouts while fetching holdings data. On timeout, user-context-service executed fallback logic that cached empty records ('holdings=0 sips=0') in the shared cache with a 6-hour TTL (21600 seconds). Subsequent assistant queries for those affected users hit these poisoned negative cache entries, causing persistent zero-holdings responses even after the upstream timeouts ceased.

Subsequent requests to user-context-service hit the poisoned cache entries, returning zero holdings to assistant-orchestrator even though portfolio-service was healthy.

# Investigation report: Assistant cannot see user holdings

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting around 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC) on 2026-09-25, users querying the AI assistant about their investments were told they have no holdings, while the Portfolio screen showed accurate holdings. Between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, user-context-service experienced transient timeouts while fetching holdings data. On timeout, user-context-service executed fallback logic that cached empty records ('holdings=0 sips=0') in the shared cache with a 6-hour TTL (21600 seconds). Subsequent assistant queries for those affected users hit these poisoned negative cache entries, causing persistent zero-holdings responses even after the upstream timeouts ceased.

**Root cause:** user-context-service wrote empty fallback contexts ('holdings=0 sips=0') into the Redis cache keyspace with an excessive 6-hour (21600s) TTL during a transient upstream fetch timeout period between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC. Subsequent requests to user-context-service hit the poisoned cache entries, returning zero holdings to assistant-orchestrator even though portfolio-service was healthy.

## Hypotheses
1. **During a transient timeout period fetching holdings from portfolio-service, user-context-service cached empty fallback records (holdings=0, sips=0) into the cache keyspace with a 6-hour TTL (21600s), poisoning the context cache for affected users.** — `user-context-service`, cache_or_staleness, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_2, ev_10, ev_12, ev_16, ev_18] · Contradicting: none
   - Logs in ev_10 and ev_12 show user-context-service directly executing 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)' on timeout. ev_2 demonstrates missing_context_rate spiked during the 08:50-09:22 UTC timeout window and remained elevated at ~8% through 11:45 UTC due to the 6-hour TTL. Meanwhile, ev_16 confirms portfolio-service latency remained normal, explaining why the Portfolio screen is unaffected.
2. **Ongoing upstream portfolio-service failure or persistent connection degradation between assistant-orchestrator and user-context-service.** — `portfolio-service`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.10, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_10] · Contradicting: [ev_1, ev_14, ev_16]
   - user-context-service error rates returned to baseline (~0.3%) by 09:25 UTC (ev_1), assistant-orchestrator error rates remained steady at ~0.5% throughout (ev_14), and portfolio-service p95 latency remained normal at 118-151 ms (ev_16), contradicting any ongoing portfolio-service outage.
3. **assistant-orchestrator software deployment regression or prompt/tool schema bug causing dropped context.** — `assistant-orchestrator`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: none · Contradicting: [ev_5, ev_6, ev_8, ev_9, ev_14]
   - No releases or config changes were deployed to assistant-orchestrator on 2026-09-25 (ev_5). The orchestrator experienced no context-retrieval errors or abnormal error rate increases (ev_6, ev_8, ev_9, ev_14).

## Facts
- No deployments or config changes were performed on assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache on 2026-09-25 prior to or during the incident. [ev_5, ev_7, ev_13]
- user-context-service error_rate spiked from baseline ~0.3% to over 10% between 08:50 UTC and 09:20 UTC, returning to normal baseline (~0.3%) by 09:25 UTC. [ev_1]
- user-context-service logged 193 instances of 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready' between 08:50:18 UTC and 09:21:57 UTC. [ev_10]
- On context build timeout, user-context-service executed 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)' writes into the shared cache. [ev_10, ev_12]
- user-context-service missing_context_rate jumped from 0.8% to 20.46% at 09:05 UTC and remained continuously elevated between 7% and 8.7% through 11:45 UTC. [ev_2]
- portfolio-service p95 latency remained normal and steady between 118.6 ms and 151.8 ms throughout the entire window. [ev_16]
- Cache hit rate in the user_context keyspace increased from ~94.8% prior to 08:50 UTC to ~98.5%-99.2% after 09:10 UTC and remained elevated through 11:45 UTC. [ev_18]
- assistant-orchestrator error rate stayed flat at ~0.50% across the incident with no context-related log warnings or errors. [ev_3, ev_6, ev_8, ev_9, ev_14]

## Inferences
- The prolonged nature of the incident ('not going away') despite transient timeout resolution at 09:22 UTC is directly caused by the 6-hour (21600-second) TTL set on fallback empty contexts. [ev_1, ev_2, ev_10, ev_12]
- Only users who triggered context builds during the 08:50 to 09:22 UTC timeout window had their cache entries poisoned, explaining why the symptom affected 'some users' rather than the entire user base. [ev_2, ev_10, ev_12]
- portfolio-service itself was functioning correctly, allowing users on the Portfolio screen to view their investments normally while assistant responses were degraded by the cached fallback context. [ev_16, ev_17]

## Assumptions
- The assistant orchestrator directly incorporates the user context holdings payload from user-context-service into its prompt without independent holdings re-verification.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-25 14:15 IST (08:45 UTC)** knowledge-index deployed CHG-48223; user-context-service and assistant-orchestrator operating at normal baseline. [ev_1, ev_2, ev_7]
- **2026-09-25 14:20:03 IST (08:50:03 UTC)** Onset of timeouts: user-context-service begins experiencing context build timeouts on holdings fetch and writes empty fallback records ('holdings=0 sips=0') to Redis with ttl=21600s. [ev_1, ev_10, ev_12]
- **2026-09-25 14:35 IST (09:05 UTC)** user-context-service error_rate peaks at 10.32% and missing_context_rate peaks at 20.46%. [ev_1, ev_2]
- **2026-09-25 14:52 IST (09:22 UTC)** Last timeout and fallback write logged by user-context-service; transient timeout window ends. [ev_10, ev_12]
- **2026-09-25 14:55 IST (09:25 UTC)** user-context-service error_rate returns to baseline (~0.31%), but missing_context_rate remains elevated at ~8% due to cached empty fallback records. [ev_1, ev_2]
- **2026-09-25 16:30 IST (11:00 UTC)** Incident INC-3320 reported by Support team lead as assistant continues to report zero holdings for affected users. [ev_2]
- **2026-09-25 17:15 IST (11:45 UTC)** Investigation window closes; missing_context_rate persists at 8.03% with elevated cache hit rate (~99%) as poisoned keys have not expired. [ev_2, ev_18]

## Confidence
0.95: Direct log evidence shows the exact fallback operation caching holdings=0 with a 21600-second TTL at the exact onset timestamp, correlating directly with the sustained 8% missing_context_rate and the lack of latency degradation in portfolio-service.

## Gaps
- Direct inspection of individual Redis keys in the user_ctx keyspace to check remaining TTL and exact payloads. (impact: Minimal; user-context-service application logs explicitly record the exact Redis SET command string, key format, payload, and TTL.)
- Root cause of the initial transient connection/readiness failure between user-context-service and portfolio-service pods during 08:50-09:22 UTC. (impact: Minor for immediate mitigation (flushing cache and fixing TTL bug), but relevant for preventing future upstream transient timeouts.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Purge or invalidate poisoned user_ctx:* keys in Redis that were written between 08:50 UTC and 09:22 UTC with fallback zero holdings. [ev_2, ev_12]
  - Why: Eliminates remaining poisoned cache entries immediately, allowing affected users to fetch live holdings from portfolio-service.
  - Verify: Check user-context-service missing_context_rate metric drops from ~8% back to baseline (<1%) and verify assistant correctly answers holdings queries for affected users.
- **[next]** Update user-context-service fallback behavior to either avoid caching negative fallback responses entirely or set a short TTL (e.g. 15-30 seconds) on timeout fallbacks. [ev_10, ev_12]
  - Why: Prevents transient downstream or network hiccups from poisoning user context cache for 6 hours.
  - Verify: Simulate timeout in staging and verify fallback cache entries have a short TTL and do not persist across normal queries once connectivity restores.
- **[later]** Investigate pod readiness and network connection pool between user-context-service and portfolio-service during 08:50-09:22 UTC. [ev_10]
  - Why: Underlying logs indicated '# of # pods ready' and holdings fetch pending timeouts; identifying why pods became unready will prevent recurring transient spikes.
  - Verify: Review Kubernetes pod events, container restart metrics, and gRPC/HTTP client timeout configurations.

Cited evidence: ev_1, ev_2, ev_3, ev_5, ev_6, ev_7, ev_8, ev_9, ev_10, ev_12, ev_13, ev_14, ev_16, ev_17, ev_18
Investigation window: 2026-09-25 13:45 IST to 2026-09-25 17:15 IST
